name: Non-deposit-taking credit provider licence/registration and conduct pack for small lenders (CBK NDTCP Regulations)
buyer: Small money lenders, asset financiers, BNPL, hire-purchase and chama-type lenders, PAYG sellers newly under CBK
trigger: Business Laws (Amendment) Act 2024 (in force 27 Dec 2024) brings all non-deposit-taking credit under CBK; draft Regulations Aug 2025; CBK impact assessment May 2026; one commentator says final regulations are LN 191 (published about 29 Sep 2026) with a six-month window to late Mar 2027; KES 20m threshold licence vs register for smaller; consumer protection, complaints, registered office duties. Many small firms would act at once at the deadline.
existing: Competitor search ('non-deposit taking credit provider licence CBK compliance software loan management reporting Kenya small lenders 2026') found no compliance software; only the CBK licence checker page (paybillke) and legal summaries. Loan-management systems exist (not checked) and may add compliance modules.
unchecked: Whether the final regulations were gazetted and the exact commencement/deadline (LinkedIn source only); periodic returns required; number of small lenders below the threshold; whether existing LMS vendors (e.g. loan-management SaaS) are adding it; CBK portal; Swahili competitor search.

first_check.duty: Business Laws (Amendment) Act 2024 / amended CBK Act s.57; CBK (Non-Deposit Taking Credit Providers) Regulations 2026, Legal Notice 191, published 29 Sep 2026 (from secondary sources; I did not open the Kenya Law or Gazette text). They revoke the 2022 DCP Regulations. Existing lenders must apply for a licence or registration within 6 months (about 29 Mar 2027) and can keep trading while CBK decides. Lenders with KES 20m or more in capital, borrowings or loan book need a licence; smaller ones register and must convert to a licence once they pass KES 20m. Fees: KES 100k application; annual KES 500k (licensed) or KES 250k (registered), due 31 Dec. Paying within 3 months after the deadline costs double; after that CBK may revoke the licence. Other duties: CBK prior approval for new products or changes (including interest rates), complaints handling and reporting, returns via the CBK BSA system (outstanding credit returns), and an annual compliance return. Coverage includes BNPL, hire purchase, P2P, PAYG and logbook lenders. Banks, microfinance banks and SACCOs are excluded.
first_check.market: 281 digital credit providers were licensed as of 28 Sep 2026, and CBK has received more than 900 DCP applications since 2022. The new regime adds a pool of offline lenders: logbook lenders, shylocks, hire purchase, BNPL and PAYG. I found no count of these. The CBK regulatory impact assessment PDF could not be parsed. Realistic addressable market: a few hundred to low thousands of firms. The KES 250k annual registration fee may push many micro lenders out or underground.
first_check.competitor: I found no dedicated NDTCP compliance or licensing-pack software. Partial substitutes: (1) The CBK online licensing portal and the BSA returns system, with CBK-run user training (CM Advocates notice). (2) Law firms that advise on licensing, such as Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr, Bowmans and CM Advocates. (3) Loan-management systems that say they cover regulatory reporting, such as SuperLMS by Super Systems (Nairobi; says it serves 40 MFIs and digital lenders), Lendsqr, Presta and Craft Silicon. LMS vendors could add a CBK module. Not checked: a Swahili-language competitor search.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Secondary sources say the CBK NDTCP Regulations 2026 are Legal Notice 191, gazetted 29 Sep 2026, with Kenya Law listing them as commenced that day. Existing lenders have six months to apply, so the deadline is about 29 Mar 2027. Lenders under KES 20m register and larger ones need a licence. Annual fees are KES 250k to register and KES 500k for a licence, and late payment costs double. Other duties: CBK approval before product changes, complaints reporting, and returns filed through CBK's BSA system. I found no dedicated compliance pack. Partial substitutes exist: law firms do licensing, the CBK portal handles applications, and loan-management vendors such as SuperLMS say they produce regulator reports. Weak points: the high fees may push out the smallest informal lenders, and those lenders are hard to reach. This is a one-off rush followed by a modest recurring need.

challenge_check.killer: None decisive. Partial substitutes: CBK's free BSA returns portal, loan-management systems such as SuperLMS that cover reporting, and law firms offering licensing work. Main risks: high fixed fees push out the smallest lenders, and licensed digital lenders are exempt from reapplying.
challenge_check.reason: No product kills it. I found no dedicated NDTCP licensing or compliance software in searches in English or Swahili. Press reports say the final rules exist as LN 191 of 2026, which gives a six-month window to about March 2027. The market is weaker than claimed for four reasons. (1) The 281 digital lenders already licensed don't need to reapply. (2) Fees are high, so the smallest lenders and chama-type lenders may stop lending rather than comply: KES 100k to apply, KES 250k a year for registration, KES 500k a year for a licence, and a KES 1m late fee. (3) Returns go through CBK's free BSA portal, and loan-management vendors already say they cover regulatory reporting. (4) Law firms already offer done-for-you licensing. The rush is a one-off; after it, the recurring work is small. I could not confirm the KES 20m threshold in the final text or the number of offline lenders.
